comments.author: frankie567
comments.body: Thank you for the very relevant comments, much appreciated 🙂 I've improved things a bit!

comments.author: eddsalkield
comments.body:
Nice improvements - thanks!  I think this is pretty near good to go.  The only other thing I thought of was quoting the strings when showing the defaults, e.g.:

> A constant `SECRET`

becomes

> A constant `"SECRET"`

or

> A constant "SECRET"

Although this is really minor, so feel free to pick whichever (that said, it's probably worth making this consistent throughout the docs.  While looking to see what is done elsewhere, it seems from the [cookie page](https://github.com/frankie567/fastapi-users/blob/dc67ebe23920070a151a01ee9f308634e258742a/docs/configuration/authentication/cookie.md) that it's a mixture of back-ticked and single-quoted).

comments.author: frankie567
comments.body: I've improved the consistency accross cookie/jwt documentation. Thank you for your help 👍

review_comments.author: eddsalkield
review_comments.body: Shouldn't the default parameter here be `tokenUrl="login"`, in accordance with the class definition?

review_comments.author: eddsalkield
review_comments.body: Perhaps specify that it should _probably_ be relative - there may be a few small use cases where people explicitly want an absolute path.

review_comments.author: eddsalkield
review_comments.body: You don't have to define three arguments - `secret` and `lifetime_seconds` are the only required arguments.  `tokenUrl` and `name` are optional.  Perhaps it's also worth mentioning the arguments by their name as well?

review_comments.author: frankie567
review_comments.body: I think it's okay to have `auth/jwt/login` because it's the working value when configuring the JWT authentication router when following the documentation. If the user follows this, it should have a working example out-of-the-box (like full examples).

review_comments.author: eddsalkield
review_comments.body: I think this can make sense, since you've specified that the `tokenUrl` "defaults to `login`".

review_comments.author: frankie567
review_comments.body: Maybe I should change the default actually 🤔

diff --git a/docs/configuration/authentication/cookie.md b/docs/configuration/authentication/cookie.md
index e3fe888a..a1040b68 100644
--- a/docs/configuration/authentication/cookie.md
+++ b/docs/configuration/authentication/cookie.md
@@ -16,27 +16,25 @@ cookie_authentication = CookieAuthentication(secret=SECRET, lifetime_seconds=360
 auth_backends.append(cookie_authentication)
 ```
 
-As you can see, instantiation is quite simple. You just have to define a constant `SECRET` which is used to encode the token and the lifetime of the cookie (in seconds).
-
-You can also define the parameters for the generated cookie:
+As you can see, instantiation is quite simple. It accepts the following arguments:
 
+* `secret` (`str`): A constant secret which is used to encode the cookie. **Use a strong passphrase and keep it secure.**
+* `lifetime_seconds` (`int`): The lifetime of the cookie in seconds.
 * `cookie_name` (`fastapiusersauth`): Name of the cookie.
 * `cookie_path` (`/`): Cookie path.
 * `cookie_domain` (`None`): Cookie domain.
 * `cookie_secure` (`True`): Whether to only send the cookie to the server via SSL request.
 * `cookie_httponly` (`True`): Whether to prevent access to the cookie via JavaScript.
-* `cookie_samesite` (`lax`): A string that specifies the samesite strategy for the cookie. Valid values are 'lax', 'strict' and 'none'. Defaults to 'lax'. 
+* `cookie_samesite` (`lax`): A string that specifies the samesite strategy for the cookie. Valid values are `lax`, `strict` and `none`. Defaults to `lax`.
+* `name` (`Optional[str]`): Name of the backend. It's useful in the case you wish to have several backends of the same class. Each backend should have a unique name. Defaults to `cookie`.
 
-!!! tip
-    You can also optionally define the `name`. It's useful in the case you wish to have several backends of the same class. Each backend should have a unique name. **Defaults to `cookie`**.
-
-    ```py
-    cookie_authentication = CookieAuthentication(
-        secret=SECRET,
-        lifetime_seconds=3600,
-        name="my-cookie",
-    )
-    ```
+```py
+cookie_authentication = CookieAuthentication(
+    secret=SECRET,
+    lifetime_seconds=3600,
+    name="my-cookie",
+)
+```
 
 !!! tip
     The value of the cookie is actually a JWT. This authentication backend shares most of its logic with the [JWT](./jwt.md) one.

-!!! tip

+* `secret` (`str`): A constant secret which is used to encode the token. **Use a strong passphrase and keep it secure.**
+* `lifetime_seconds` (`int`): The lifetime of the token in seconds.
+* `tokenUrl` (`Optional[str]`): The exact path of your login endpoint. It'll allow the interactive documentation to automatically discover it and get a working *Authorize* button. In most cases, you'll probably need a **relative** path, not absolute. You can read more details about this in the [FastAPI documentation](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/security/first-steps/#fastapis-oauth2passwordbearer). Defaults to `auth/jwt/login`.
+* `name` (`Optional[str]`): Name of the backend. It's useful in the case you wish to have several backends of the same class. Each backend should have a unique name. Defaults to `jwt`.
